Implemented a full Node.js CLI tool at:

- [main.js](/workspace/output/main.js)

It follows your required interface:

```bash
node output/main.js --bib <path> --style <path> [--cites <path>] [--aux <path>] --output <path> [--log <path>]
```

What’s implemented in `output/main.js`:

- CLI parsing with required flags and exit code behavior (`0/1/2`)
- `.cites` parsing (one key per line, ignores blank and `#` lines)
- `.aux` parsing for `\citation{...}` (accumulates keys)
- Cite list concatenation (`--cites` then `--aux`) and case-insensitive dedupe
- `.bib` parser:
  - `@string`, `@preamble`, `@comment`, regular entries
  - concatenated field expressions with `#`
  - predefined month macros + user macros
  - duplicate key warning
  - unresolved macro warning
  - crossref inheritance + unresolved/cycle warnings
- `.bst` parser:
  - top-level commands: `ENTRY`, `STRINGS`, `INTEGERS`, `MACRO`, `FUNCTION`, `READ`, `EXECUTE`, `ITERATE`, `REVERSE`, `SORT`
  - function bodies, string/int literals, quoted identifiers, function literals
- Stack-machine runtime:
  - built-ins listed in your summary (`if$`, `while$`, `format.name$`, `purify$`, `width$`, `write$`, `newline$`, etc.)
  - stable sort by `sort.key$`
  - entry/global variable handling and assignment
- `.bbl` output buffering and wrapping at 79 columns with continuation indent
- Structured `--log` JSON output
- Structured error JSON to `--output` on failure (with warnings included)

I also ran a local smoke test using `plain.bst` and a sample `.bib` entry to verify the command runs end-to-end and emits both output and log files.
